sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let's explore how static members work in Java - they're like shared tools for all objects of a class!

• What static variables, constants, and methods are
• How they differ from instance members
• When and how to use them effectively

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine a classroom with a whiteboard. The whiteboard is 'static' - everyone in the class can see and use it. That's exactly how static members work in Java!

Static members belong to the class itself, not individual objects. Here's what that means:

• **Static Variables**: Shared across all instances (like the classroom whiteboard)
- Declared with `static` keyword
- Only one copy exists for the entire class

• **Constants**: Special static variables that never change
- Declared with `final static`
- Named in ALL_CAPS_WITH_UNDERSCORES
- Example: `final static double PI = 3.14159;`

• **Static Methods**: Class-level functions
- Can be called without creating an object
- Example: `Math.sqrt(25)` (no Math object needed!)

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: A static variable belongs to the class and is shared among all instances
A static method can be called without creating an object: ClassName.method()
Static methods cannot access instance (non-static) data fields directly
Static constants (static final) are commonly used for shared unchanging values like Math.PI
Instance members belong to an object; static members belong to the class

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Static members belong to the class, not objects. Constants are `final static` and named in ALL_CAPS. Practice using static for shared data and utility methods. Ready to learn about visibility modifiers next.

questions.question: What does the 'static' keyword mean for a variable?
options: The variable belongs to the class and is shared by all instances
The variable is only accessible in the main method
The variable is stored on the heap
questions.explanation: A static variable belongs to the class rather than any specific instance. All objects of the class share the same static variable.

questions.question: Can you call a static method without creating an object?
options: No, an object is always required
Yes, using the class name (e.g., ClassName.method())
Only if the method is void
questions.explanation: Static methods can be called using the class name directly, without creating an instance. For example, Math.sqrt(25) calls the static sqrt method of the Math class.
